candidates.attacker_control: The attacker controls the password value presented to authentication (form login, HTTP Basic, or any other mechanism producing a UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken). The username must be known. No other request data is needed; the password just has to be the literal string "null" (or the empty string if the stored password is empty).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified DaoAuthenticationProvider really does default to PlaintextPasswordEncoder in this snapshot (line 68) and really passes userDetails.getPassword() unmodified to it (line 94). Checked that org.springframework.security.core.userdetails.User rejects null passwords, which means the null-password state requires a custom UserDetails implementation or a Jdbc-user mapping that does not use User (JdbcDaoImpl constructs new User(...), which would throw on a null column rather than authenticate). Checked that AbstractUserDetailsAuthenticationProvider rejects null credentials before additionalAuthenticationChecks, so the bypass needs a non-null presented value such as "null". Checked that the empty-string case is a plain equality match rather than a length/logic error. Looked for later or parallel implementations with the same pattern; the crypto-module MessageDigestPasswordEncoder/Md4PasswordEncoder use `"" + encPass` but the result is compared against a digest, so no equivalent bypass exists there. Did not find any framework test in the snapshot (no test sources are included) and did not execute anything, so the null-password deployment scenario remains an application-dependent condition rather than a demonstrated exploit.
candidates.impact: Authentication/authorization bypass: an unauthenticated remote user can obtain an Authentication for the affected account (with that account's authorities and, in session-based apps, a session-bound authenticated SecurityContext), enabling account takeover and access to every resource/permission granted to that account. The same code path also allows login with an empty password against an account whose stored password is empty.
candidates.prerequisites: Application is on the 4.2.x line and uses the default DaoAuthenticationProvider configuration (PlaintextPasswordEncoder), or explicitly configures PlaintextPasswordEncoder/plaintext `password-encoder` for that provider. A target account must return null or the empty string from UserDetails#getPassword() at authentication time (e.g. a custom UserDetailsService/UserDetails implementation, legacy/placeholder rows, or an account provisioned for non-password authentication), and that account must pass the enabled/locked/expired pre-authentication checks. The bundled org.springframework.security.core.userdetails.User constructor rejects null passwords (line 112) but permits the empty string, so the null case requires a custom UserDetails implementation.
candidates.root_cause: PlaintextPasswordEncoder.isPasswordValid builds the stored side of the comparison as `String pass1 = encPass + "";`. If the stored password is null, Java string concatenation yields the four-character literal "null"; the presented side is `mergePasswordAndSalt(rawPass, salt, false)` and the two are compared with PasswordEncoderUtils.equals. An attacker who submits the password "null" therefore produces pass2 == "null" == pass1 and is authenticated. The same method also treats an empty stored password as matching an empty submitted password. DaoAuthenticationProvider selects this encoder by default (`setPasswordEncoder(new PlaintextPasswordEncoder())`, line 68) and passes `userDetails.getPassword()` straight into it (line 94), so the defect is on the default 4.2.x authentication path, not only in optional/deprecated configuration.
candidates.title: Authentication bypass for accounts with null/empty stored password via default PlaintextPasswordEncoder in DaoAuthenticationProvider
candidates.trace: Login request -> AbstractAuthenticationProcessingFilter.attemptAuthentication -> ProviderManager -> DaoAuthenticationProvider.authenticate -> AbstractUserDetailsAuthenticationProvider.authenticate (preAuthenticationChecks) -> DaoAuthenticationProvider.additionalAuthenticationChecks (line 92: presentedPassword = credentials.toString(); line 94: passwordEncoder.isPasswordValid(userDetails.getPassword(), presentedPassword, salt)) -> PlaintextPasswordEncoder.isPasswordValid (line 54: pass1 = encPass + "" -> "null"; line 59: pass2 = mergePasswordAndSalt("null", null, false) -> "null") -> PasswordEncoderUtils.equals("null", "null") returns true -> createSuccessAuthentication returns an authenticated token and the request is treated as the target user.
candidates.unverified: It is not established from source alone that this is the specific historically fixed issue for this snapshot/version, nor that any real application returns a null (as opposed to empty) password from UserDetails; the exact upstream fix contents and the CVE mapping could not be inspected (no network, no patch, no tests). The candidate is a source-evidence-based lead, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability.

coverage_summary: Scope: 1317 model-visible files at the assigned source root, no symlink/oversize/sensitive-name exclusions; the P1 relation index is complete (1317/1317 files indexed, 8594 symbols, 13578 edges, hash mismatches 0) and was used for navigation only, not as a verdict; it contains no SAST oracle, no data/control-flow, and no proof of reachability. Reviewed by reading source: authentication providers and password encoders (core/authentication/**, crypto/password/**, crypto/bcrypt, crypto/scrypt, crypto/encrypt), DaoAuthenticationProvider and AbstractUserDetailsAuthenticationProvider, the default encoder wiring, remember-me (AbstractRememberMeServices, TokenBased/PersistentTokenBased/Jdbc/InMemory), anonymous/remember-me/basic/digest providers and filters, web context persistence, session/session-fixation and concurrent-session handling, CSRF filter and repositories, HTTP firewalls and request/response wrappers, request matchers and URL utilities, filter security interceptor and ExceptionTranslationFilter, method security metadata/voters, ldap (AbstractLdapAuthenticationProvider, BindAuthenticator, ActiveDirectory*, PasswordComparisonAuthenticator, LdapEncoder), cas, openid, messaging, taglibs, acl, and parts of config (HttpSecurity/WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter defaults, CsrfConfigurer, CorsConfigurer, LdapAuthenticationProviderConfigurer). Not exhaustively reviewed line-by-line: large sample/application trees (samples/**, sandbox/**), build/Gradle/POM and doc files, messaging/socket and webmvc-integration details, aspects module, and the full bodies of the biggest classes listed above; no tests are present in the snapshot and no code, tests, scanners or payloads were executed.
limitations: No test sources are included in the snapshot, so intended behavior could not be cross-checked against repository tests.
Nothing was compiled or executed; all conclusions are static source readings, and no runtime confirmation or exploitability proof exists.
The relation index provides only syntactic navigation candidates and does not prove call reachability or data flow; edges cited here were re-verified in source text where used.

The mapping of this snapshot to a specific historical security fix/CVE could not be verified without network, patch, or advisory access; the submitted candidate may not be the issue the snapshot was selected for.

Reachability of the null-password scenario depends on application code (custom UserDetails / non-standard user storage) that is not part of this repository, and the bundled User class forbids null passwords, so real-world triggerability is unproven.
Large portions of the tree (samples, sandbox, build scripts, and unexamined methods in very large classes) were not read exhaustively; absence of a finding there is not evidence of absence.

rejected_leads.lead: DelegatingPasswordEncoder.matches(CharSequence, String) returns true when both rawPassword and prefixEncodedPassword are null (crypto/src/main/java/org/springframework/security/crypto/password/DelegatingPasswordEncoder.java lines 190-193).
rejected_leads.reason: Confirmed in source, but within the framework the only production caller is DaoAuthenticationProvider, which rejects a null presented credential before invoking the encoder, and every other encoder implementation either returns false or throws on null input; no in-repo caller can supply two nulls, so I could not construct a reachable authentication impact from source alone.

rejected_leads.lead: Several crypto password encoders (MessageDigestPasswordEncoder, Md4PasswordEncoder, StandardPasswordEncoder, Pbkdf2PasswordEncoder) lack the null/empty 'Empty encoded password' guard that BCryptPasswordEncoder and SCryptPasswordEncoder already have.
rejected_leads.reason: The observable effects are unchecked exceptions (NPE / ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException / NumberFormatException) on malformed or null stored values, i.e. per-request error handling rather than an authentication bypass or a demonstrable confidentiality/integrity impact; the encoded side of the comparison normally comes from trusted storage.

rejected_leads.lead: LdapShaPasswordEncoder (crypto) accepts an empty encoded password as a match for an empty raw password via PasswordEncoderUtils.equals.
rejected_leads.reason: This is ordinary string equality between the stored value and the submitted value, so it requires the application to have stored an empty password for the account; no evidence in the snapshot that this is the intended target, and it cannot be distinguished from intended plaintext-fallback behavior described in the class javadoc.

rejected_leads.lead: LDAP empty-password (unauthenticated bind) handling in the ldap module.
rejected_leads.reason: Already guarded in this snapshot: AbstractLdapAuthenticationProvider.authenticate rejects !StringUtils.hasLength(password) (lines 77-81) and BindAuthenticator rejects empty passwords (lines 77-81), so no bypass was found there.

rejected_leads.lead: Session fixation, CSRF, remember-me token generation, HTTP firewall (StrictHttpFirewall/DefaultHttpFirewall/RequestWrapper/FirewalledResponse), AntPathRequestMatcher, ExceptionTranslationFilter, FilterSecurityInterceptor, CSRF cookie repository, and redirect/target-URL handling.
rejected_leads.reason: These were read and matched the expected 4.2.x semantics (session strategy invoked before successfulAuthentication, non-GET CSRF enforcement, SecureRandom token generation, path normalization/blacklists, constant-time remember-me signature comparison, no CRLF in headers); no source-backed defect was identified, so they are unconfirmed leads rather than candidates.

summary: Spring Security 4.2.13.BUILD-SNAPSHOT source snapshot (4.2.x maintenance branch; POMs still pin 4.2.12.RELEASE). I reviewed authentication/authorization flows across core, web, crypto, config, ldap, cas, openid, messaging, taglibs and acl, using the P1 relation index for navigation only and verifying every candidate against source text. The one candidate I can defend from source is a null/empty stored-password handling defect in the deprecated plaintext encoder that is the default password encoder of DaoAuthenticationProvider on this branch: `encPass + ""` turns a null stored password into the literal string "null", which `PasswordEncoderUtils.equals` then matches against a submitted password of "null", so accounts whose UserDetails#getPassword() is null (or empty) can authenticate without a real credential. I could not confirm this is the historical CVE associated with this version, and reachability depends on an application returning null/empty passwords from its UserDetails implementation, so confidence is low. Other plausible leads were checked and rejected (see rejected_leads). No tests are present in the snapshot and nothing was executed.
